sources.entry: traceAI - Open-source OpenTelemetry-native tracing framework for LLM and AI agent applications. Auto-instruments 20+ frameworks (OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Bedrock).

summary.one_liner: traceAI is an open-source, OpenTelemetry-native tracing library that instruments LLM calls, prompts, tokens, retrieval steps and agent actions in Python, TypeScript, Java and C# and sends them to any OTel-compatible backend.
summary.what_it_does: traceAI provides drop-in instrumentation packages that wrap LLM provider SDKs, agent frameworks, MCP, voice tools and vector databases so their calls are recorded as OpenTelemetry spans. Captured data includes prompts and completions, token counts, model parameters, tool calls and arguments, streaming chunks, errors, and per-step timing, following OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions. The README lists packages for Python (for example traceai-openai, traceai-langchain), TypeScript (@traceai/*), Java (traceai-java-*) and C# (fi-instrumentation-otel). Traces are exported via standard OTLP HTTP or gRPC to backends such as Datadog, Grafana, Jaeger or Future AGI. The README also shows how to attach traceAI to a custom TracerProvider and span processor.
use_cases: trace LLM calls and token usage in production
debug RAG retrieval or tool-call failures in agents
send AI traces to an existing Datadog or Grafana setup
instrument OpenAI or Anthropic code with minimal changes
monitor vector database queries in AI apps
add observability to Spring AI or LangChain4j apps
how_to_run: Set FI_API_KEY, FI_SECRET_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY environment variables
notable: Instruments 50+ AI frameworks and providers across four languages with a consistent API
Vendor-neutral: exports standard OTLP traces to any OpenTelemetry backend rather than requiring a new dashboard
Covers vector databases (Pinecone, Qdrant, pgvector and others) alongside LLM providers and agent frameworks
Compatibility matrix in the README shows which framework is available in which language
Custom TracerProvider and span processor setup is documented for BYO OpenTelemetry configurations
caveats: Quickstart examples use Future AGI keys (FI_API_KEY, FI_SECRET_KEY) for the default register() path, though the README says traces work with other backends
Compatibility is uneven: many frameworks are Python-only, and Go support is listed only on the roadmap
Sampling strategies and evaluation integration are roadmap items, not current features
